title: The Function of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a society's structured ranking that is exercised by a variety of persons and groups. It involves systems where individuals are assigned varying levels of wealth, power, and prestige, which affects life opportunities regardless of individual merit or effort.

Functionalist perspectives often suggest that stratification serves a purpose: highly skilled positions require greater rewards to incentivize capable individuals to fill them. Conversely, conflict theories argue that these hierarchies are maintained by those in power to justify unequal distribution of resources and maintain the status quo.
